subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` object, or should send/read/list separation be handled by the adjacent A2A allowlist and per-agent visibility proposals instead?
rationale: This changes the public config shape and cross-agent transcript privacy boundary, and several open related proposals overlap the same authorization surface without one settled model.

options.title: Approve Unified Capability Object
options.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send, history, list, and metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

options.title: Use A2A And Allowlist Scopes
options.body: Make the adjacent A2A or allowlist proposals canonical if maintainers decide they satisfy the send-without-read privacy goal without a new capability object.

options.title: Hold For Related PR Decisions
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design question while the overlapping open PRs are reviewed or closed.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Capability Object
recommendation.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send, history, list, and metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the strongest owner for the public session-tool config, schema, docs, and security-scoping boundary this decision changes.
